name: Prize crossword No 22,273
preamble: Method: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: Left (say) in peace at last from swift attack

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to hear the word peace spoken, where it matches a word for a portion
'in' places the letter for left inside the letters that the word peace leads to

blocks.note: peace sounds like piece, and a piece is a bit
L is the standard abbreviation for left
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be left in peace at last after a sudden assault.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into BIT, then Z, the alphabet's last letter, is added to make BLITZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is a sudden intensive military onslaught, the German word for lightning used for rapid warfare.

clue.text: Runners' event made odd bod germinate

indicators.note: to make something odd is to render it strange, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A strange chap is sprouting at an athletics fixture for runners.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners here are not athletes but the people who run a company, the directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Company directors run the firm, and their gathering around the table is a formal session of the board.

clue.text: Redwood I'm not: each part's in other clue

definitions.text: Redwood I'm not: each part's in other clue

blocks.note: surface reading: a tree insisting it is not a sequoia
setter's reading: a pale-timbered plant whose two halves each turn up as words in the clues to 20 and 21

explanation.walkthrough: Ivory is white, the opposite of red, so its wood is no redwood; the word ivory is in 20's clue and Trees opens 21's.
explanation.definitionFit: The ivory-tree is an Indian shrub with pale white timber, so it names a tree whose wood is anything but red.

clue.text: Ends end with forger: WT's her title

definitions.note: describes the author through her novel's title

blocks.note: the two ends of the alphabet
to die is to come to an end
a smith forges metal at the forge

explanation.surface: A note about a crook's undoing, signed off with initials and a title.
explanation.walkthrough: WT is White Teeth, the answer at 20/17: ZADIE SMITH wrote it. The forger is a metalworker, not a counterfeiter.
explanation.definitionFit: White Teeth was the celebrated first novel of this British writer, so its title belongs to her.

clue.text: Memory first held by friend in shiny plate

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so these letters go within the word for friend

blocks.note: a chum is a friend
ROM is read-only memory in computing
I is the Roman numeral one, i.e. first

explanation.surface: A memento of a friend kept on a gleaming plate.
explanation.walkthrough: First is I, the Roman one; memory is computing's read-only kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromium is the bright metal used for plating car trim and taps, giving a mirror finish.

clue.text: Vessel - pay in a pound first - limits cruise

blocks.note: a can is a container
taken as written
L is the sign for a pound sterling
to bank money is to pay it in

explanation.surface: A boat trip: put a pound in first, and the vessel is restricted on its cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells us A and L come before the word for pay in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise along a waterway is hemmed in on either side by its embankments, the edges of the cut.

clue.text: The bird that, as they say, 'll be after cast

definitions.text: that, as they say, 'll be after cast
definitions.note: a cryptic route to the chess piece

indicators.note: 'as they say' asks us to hear the words spoken rather than read them

blocks.note: first meaning: a black crow that nests in colonies

blocks.clueFragment: that, as they say, 'll be after cast
blocks.note: second meaning: cast followed by 'll sounds like castle, and a castle is another name for a particular chess piece

explanation.surface: A riddle about a bird that will turn up once the cast has been chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast + 'll spoken aloud is castle, and a castle in chess is also called a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: Rook is both a black corvid of the farmland and the chess piece shaped like a tower or castle.

clue.text: French walls where s-summer haunts of flies were (Keats)

definitions.note: the clue gives the adjective Keats used for those haunts

blocks.note: mur is French for wall; two of them make walls
où is French for where, carrying on the French theme
the stammered first letter

explanation.surface: A Keats-tinged picture of a summer spot buzzing with flies by old French walls.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's Ode to a Nightingale has 'The murmurous haunt of flies on summer eves'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ode the poet calls the summer haunt of flies murmurous, meaning filled with a low humming sound.

clue.text: Not fit for doze, which former note is spanning

indicators.note: a thing spanning another stretches across it, so it wraps around it

blocks.note: ut is the old name for the note now called do
a nap is a doze

explanation.surface: Someone is too unfit even for a snooze, which an old musical note stretches across.
explanation.walkthrough: UT was the first syllable of the old sol-fa scale, later replaced by do.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt is an uncommon word meaning unsuitable or ill-adapted to some purpose.

clue.text: I'll whisper: first, Loud Noise each way you back

definitions.note: a phrase said instead of whispering

indicators.note: 'each way' has one word for noise going backwards and the other forwards

blocks.note: A is the top grade, first class
a row is a noisy din
a din is a loud noise
taken as written
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A speaker promises to whisper, then lists a loud noise both ways and your backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Loud Noise supplies two noises, ROW and DIN, one read each way.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'a word in your ear' introduces a private confidential remark, much like murmuring something quietly to someone.

clue.text: Non-local shoppers shake - Sting's in the show

indicators.note: to shake is to jumble, so the letters of the singer's name are rearranged
'in' places the rearranged letters inside the word for show

blocks.note: a parade is a public show
the singer's name with its S

explanation.surface: Shoppers from out of town are shaken because the rock star Sting is in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting's apostrophe-S counts as a letter, giving six to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing trade is business from customers who happen to be going by rather than regular local buyers.

clue.text: Seems prisoners (done for battery?) get no booze

definitions.note: the question mark flags the pun on battery

blocks.note: to be dry is to go without alcohol
cells are where prisoners are kept

explanation.surface: Inmates convicted of assault apparently have to go without drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery means assault in law and a power source in electronics; the parenthesis is a hint that the second sense is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch battery is built from units holding a moist paste electrolyte, the kind called dry, unlike wet accumulators.

clue.text: High in amount prescribed indeed in past

indicators.note: 'in' places the letter for high within the word for an allotted amount

blocks.note: a quota is a prescribed share
H is the abbreviation for high

explanation.surface: Being high within a prescribed dose was, indeed, a thing of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Quotha is an archaic sarcastic interjection meaning 'said he!' or 'indeed!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old writers used quotha as a scornful exclamation, roughly a former way of saying 'forsooth' or 'really!'.

clue.text: Lord! Unknown number quite adds hours to day

blocks.note: an earl is a lord
y is an algebraic unknown
C is the Roman numeral 100
all can mean quite, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A lord exclaims that an unknown number of extra hours have been added to his day.
explanation.definitionFit: Being woken at dawn by an alarm request extends your waking time, lengthening the working schedule.

clue.text: You nearly get the sack from Jack's recital

indicators.note: 'nearly' means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
to be given the heave-ho is to be dismissed

explanation.surface: A sailor's speech nearly gets you fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor (Jack tar); 'yo-heave-ho' is the chant sung by sailors hauling ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen chanted this refrain while hauling together, so it is what a sailor recites at work.

clue.text: Yearn first for grain for coleopteron

blocks.note: to long is to yearn
I is the Roman numeral one
corn is grain

explanation.surface: Someone yearns first for grain, which turns out to be beetle food.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleoptera are beetles; longicorns are beetles with very long antennae, often called longhorn beetles.

clue.text: Who regulates makes what not quite safe go

indicators.note: 'not quite' means the word falls one letter short of complete
asking what something makes invites us to rebuild the letters into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about who makes sure something not quite safe can go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: OFGAS was the UK's Office of Gas Supply, the watchdog of the gas industry (later merged into Ofgem).
explanation.definitionFit: This British government body supervised the supply of household gas, so it is an industry regulator.

clue.text: The sticky stuff needs smoothing tool, my duck

blocks.note: goo is sticky stuff
a sander smooths wood

explanation.surface: A DIYer tells their darling that the glue needs sanding down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My duck' sounds like a term of endearment ('duck' is British slang for dear), but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a large fish-eating sawbill of the merganser family, a diving waterbird.

clue.text: See 20
West Indian capital, West there or gone

blocks.note: first meaning: the capital of St Vincent and the Grenadines
second meaning: the westward town still stands there, or the Irish harbour town of the name has gone

explanation.walkthrough: The Irish port south of Dublin was renamed Dún Laoghaire in 1920, so that name has gone, while the Caribbean one remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Caribbean seat of government in St Vincent and to a former Irish ferry port.

clue.text: Cardinal Noggs now fit to do fresh feats

definitions.text: now fit to do fresh feats

blocks.note: first meaning: John Henry ..., the Victorian churchman made a cardinal
... Noggs, the clerk in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby

blocks.clueFragment: now fit to do fresh feats
blocks.note: third meaning: someone restored to vigour feels like a different person

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: the cardinal, Dickens's Noggs, and the feeling of being reborn.
explanation.definitionFit: After recovering, one feels like a renewed person; the cardinal and Dickens's clerk both bore this name.

clue.text: The English wit, the work in ivory

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English humorist's literary output, carved in ivory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The work' also hints at the novel itself, Zadie Smith's White Teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories is a jokey word for a set of teeth, which are pale white like elephant tusk.

clue.text: Trees followed with discretion start to play

blocks.note: firs are trees
tact is discretion

explanation.surface: Trees, handled discreetly, begin the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama opens with its initial section, the opening division of a stage play.

clue.text: See 3
This little lad will tell you what's not true

definitions.text: will tell you what's not true

blocks.note: first meaning: a pet form of Joshua

blocks.clueFragment: will tell you what's not true
blocks.note: second meaning: to tease someone with fibs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fibbing child; the second meaning is a verb for kidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Josh is the familiar short form of Joshua, and to josh is to kid or banter with playful untruths.

clue.text: What's wrong, lad? Naught? Locate first one - Lord Canning

blocks.note: a vice is a wrong
a boy's name
the circle for zero
to locate is to find
the Roman numeral
A is first-class, A1

explanation.surface: A worried question to a boy about nothing, then a search for the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Canning, Earl Canning, governed India after the 1857 rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Canning became the first British ruler of India to hold the title of the Crown's representative there, in 1858.

clue.text: Mark front page back, unpaid: hence twice "The Sea!"

definitions.note: names the man by his famous cry rather than plainly

indicators.note: 'back' says the phrase for front page is read from its end

blocks.note: a cross is a mark
page one, written as P ONE
honorary, as in an unpaid post

explanation.surface: A note on a newspaper: mark the front page, unpaid, and hence a sea cry.
explanation.walkthrough: In Xenophon's Anabasis the Greek army, reaching the Black Sea, shout 'Thalatta! Thalatta!' — 'The sea! The sea!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek historian recorded the soldiers' double shout on sighting the coast after their long march home.

clue.text: Fit the right shoe: this one may bring you luck

definitions.text: Fit the right shoe: this one may bring you luck

blocks.note: surface reading: advice on choosing footwear

blocks.clueFragment: this one may bring you luck
blocks.note: setter's reading: the right shoe joined to the animal gives the lucky charm hung over doors

explanation.walkthrough: The animal that wears an iron shoe; add shoe to the answer and you get the traditional good-luck charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal put in front of shoe forms the lucky charm, a horseshoe nailed above a door for fortune.
